note.note:
Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  - Acute, severe headache with visual changes and vomiting; no specific trigger or exposure identified.
- Symptom timeline and progression:
  - Onset: sudden this morning, approximately 4 hours prior to consult.
  - Progression: started suddenly, remains ongoing; movement/standing worsens symptoms.
  - Severity: patient rates pain ~6/10 (compared to prior kidney stone as 10/10).
- ENT symptoms:
  - Throat swelling/closure sensation: none reported.
  - Voice change/hoarseness: none reported.
  - Dysphagia/odynophagia/drooling: none reported.
  - Nasal/ocular symptoms: blurred vision with “zigzag lines” (visual disturbance described).
  - Stridor/noisy breathing/dyspnea: none reported.
  - Distribution of swelling (lips/tongue/uvula/face): none reported.
  - Ear/neck symptoms: none reported.
- Other neurological/associated symptoms:
  - Dizziness reported.
  - Nausea and vomiting: vomited twice at onset; ongoing nausea, feels likely to vomit again.
  - No weakness in arms or legs; gait normal per patient.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
  - No prior similar headache episodes reported; patient states this is a new presentation.
  - Past medical history: history of kidney stones (patient comparison pain to kidney stone).
  - Family history: mother with migraines and hypothyroidism.
  - No prior hospitalizations or injection therapy for this problem documented.
- Allergies and current medications:
  - Allergies: “Not that I’m aware” (no known drug allergies documented).
  - Current regular medications: none reported.
  - Rescue/acute medications tried: paracetamol taken ~1 hour after onset (timing: headache started ~4 hours ago; paracetamol taken ~3 hours ago) — paracetamol did not help. (Dose/route/frequency not documented.)
- Social context:
  - No pregnancy suspected by patient (“I really doubt it”).
  - Call briefly lost during the consult; no accompaniment noted.

Objective:
- Observable swelling and distribution: none stated.
- Airway/breathing descriptors: no stridor or breathing difficulty reported.
- Mental status and associated features: patient alert; dizzy and nauseated; no syncope reported.
- Vitals and examination findings: Not recorded.
- Presence of another person with the patient: Not stated.
- Technical/connection note: brief loss of connection during consult.

Assessment:
- Clinical impression:
  - Probable migraine headache with visual aura and associated nausea/vomiting.
- Key justifications from transcript:
  - Sudden onset unilateral (left-sided) headache, blurred vision with zigzag lines (visual disturbance/aura), nausea and vomiting, worsened by movement—all features consistent with migraine.
- Uncertainty/conflicts noted:
  - Conflict noted: location described as “behind the eye” at one point and later patient stated uncertainty about precise location (“no, no... I don't know how to describe it”).
  - Family thyroid history: doctor briefly misstated “hyperthyroid” before patient clarified “hypothyroidism” in mother — conflict noted.

Plan:
- Immediate actions taken/advised:
  - Advised to try symptomatic treatment: ibuprofen and an anti-sickness medication (specific antiemetic name/dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Advised to try a sugary, carbonated drink (e.g., Coke) as part of initial symptomatic management.
- Specific instructions provided to patient:
  - If symptoms improve after treatment and before the planned assessment, patient may cancel the appointment by calling the clinic.
  - If symptoms persist or worsen, return for further evaluation.
  - “If any further problems between now and your appointment, please do let us know.” (patient instructed to contact clinic)
- Escalation criteria / red flags instructed:
  - Implicit escalation to urgent assessment/ED if headache is really severe or if symptoms do not improve; doctor indicated need for full neurological examination if medications do not help.
  - Explicit red-flag features to seek urgent care not itemized in transcript beyond above; typical concerns discussed by patient included worry about stroke/brain tumor and doctor advised further assessment if severe.
- Follow-up:
  - Arranged clinic assessment later the same day (appointment to perform full neurological exam); patient to attend or cancel if improved.
  - Discussion of step-up migraine treatments if initial measures fail (details not documented).
- COVID-19 vaccine suitability: not discussed.
- Emergency contact instructions (as stated):
  - “If any further problems between now and your appointment, please do let us know.” (no emergency number or EMS instruction documented)

Document_quality / Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vital signs (BP, HR, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, temperature) — Not recorded.
  - Neurological examination findings (cranial nerve exam, motor/sensory signs, coordination) — Not performed or not documented.
  - Fundoscopic exam or assessment for papilledema — Not recorded.
  - Photophobia/phonophobia details and detailed aura timing/duration — Not documented.
  - Specific antiemetic name, and doses/routes/frequencies for recommended analgesic/antiemetic — Not documented.
  - Pregnancy test or confirmation despite patient’s comment — Not documented.
  - Past personal history of migraines or prior similar episodes with dates/treatment — patient denies prior episodes; no past migraine treatment history documented.
  - Clear written escalation/emergency contact instructions (e.g., call EMS/911) — Not documented.
  - Allergies list confirmed in chart (only patient report recorded).
  - Plan for imaging (CT/MRI) if red flags persist — Not documented.
- Internal conflicts from transcript:
  - Location of pain: described as “behind the eye” at one point, later patient uncertain — conflict noted.
  - Doctor’s initial misstatement of family thyroid disorder as “hyperthyroid” vs patient stating mother has hypothyroidism — conflict noted.
- Transcript quality:
  - Brief loss of connection during the consult noted; otherwise content intelligible.
